blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the annual budget is a commitment. It is the moment the whole company agrees on what it will try to do, what it will stop doing, and how success will be measured. Done well, it aligns thousands of daily decisions around a small number of clear goals. Done badly, it becomes an administrative ritual that everybody resents and nobody believes.

The senior leader's task is to protect the seriousness of the budget conversation. That means pushing back politely but firmly when a proposed number is fantasy, when an assumption is soft, or when a target has been quietly adjusted between the first draft and the final version without anyone noticing.

Every senior finance leader should treat the budget as a negotiation between the company and its own future — not as a form to be filled in. The ones who do produce budgets the organisation actually uses to decide. The ones who do not produce documents that sit on a shared drive, consulted briefly in February and quietly ignored from April onward.

items.q: According to the text, what is the annual budget at senior level?
items.why: "At senior level, the annual budget is a commitment."

items.q: What is described as the senior leader's task?
options: To reduce the size of the finance team
To approve the first draft quickly
To protect the seriousness of the budget conversation
items.why: "The senior leader's task is to protect the seriousness of the budget conversation."

items.q: The author says a well-made budget aligns daily decisions around…
options: a detailed list of departmental rules
a small number of clear goals
the preferences of the finance team
items.why: "it aligns thousands of daily decisions around a small number of clear goals."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A budget is a serious negotiation with the future.
Once approved, a budget is essentially a form and can be set aside.
Soft assumptions deserve to be challenged.
Quiet changes between drafts should be explained.
items.why: Inferência: o texto ataca justamente a ideia do orçamento como formulário a ser preenchido e depois ignorado.

items.q: The phrase "consulted briefly in February and quietly ignored from April onward" suggests that…
options: February is the busiest month for finance
a weak budget stops guiding decisions almost as soon as the year begins
the company changes its fiscal year
items.why: Inferência: a imagem mostra um orçamento que perde relevância logo no início do ano — ninguém decide por ele.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James conduzindo a revisão do orçamento. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Before we approve anything, I want to pause on two lines. Between the first draft and the version in front of us, the revenue target went up by four percent and the marketing spend came down by nearly the same amount. Nobody flagged either change, and I only caught them by comparing the two files line by line.

Now, I'm not saying the new numbers are wrong. What I'm saying is that a four percent swing on that scale is not a rounding error — it's a decision. And if it's a decision, someone made it, and I'd like to understand the reasoning before we sign off.

My concern is simple. If we let numbers move quietly between drafts, we teach the whole organisation that the budget is negotiable after the fact. Six months from now, when a region misses its target, they'll point back to a number nobody can explain, and we'll have no ground to stand on.

So here's what I'd like. Whoever adjusted these two lines, walk me through the assumption behind each. If the case is solid, we approve today. If it's soft, we hold and firm it up. Either way, the change gets written down — with a name against it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What two changes did James notice between the drafts?
options: The tax rate and the currency assumption changed
Marketing spend rose and revenue fell
The revenue target rose and marketing spend fell
Headcount rose and travel spend fell
items.why: "the revenue target went up by four percent and the marketing spend came down by nearly the same amount."

items.q: How did James discover the changes?
options: Someone flagged them in the meeting
By comparing the two files line by line
items.why: "I only caught them by comparing the two files line by line."

items.q: Why does James call a four percent swing "a decision"?
options: Because it exceeds the audit threshold
Because four percent is the company's target margin
Because a change of that size is too large to be an accident and someone must have made it
Because the board must vote on any change
items.why: "a four percent swing on that scale is not a rounding error — it's a decision. And if it's a decision, someone made it."

items.q: What does James fear will happen if numbers move quietly between drafts?
options: The budget will take longer to approve
The organisation learns the budget can be renegotiated after the fact, leaving no ground to stand on later
The finance team will be blamed by the board
The software will crash during the next cycle
items.why: Inferência: ele teme que mudanças silenciosas ensinem a empresa que o número não vale — e aí ninguém sustenta a meta depois.

items.q: How would you best describe James's stance?
options: He is indifferent to the changes
He assumes the new numbers are fraudulent
He is firm about accountability but open to approving if the reasoning holds
He refuses to approve any budget this year
items.why: Inferência: ele não acusa ninguém — pede a justificativa e aprova se a premissa for sólida, mas exige que fique registrado.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The budget is a commitment, not a wish list." A commitment is…
items.why: Commitment = compromisso: uma promessa que obriga, não um desejo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good budget helps ___ thousands of daily decisions around a few clear goals."
items.why: To align = alinhar: colocar as decisões na mesma direção das metas.

items.q: "The new revenue line rests on a soft assumption." This means the assumption is…
options: weakly supported and easy to challenge
items.why: Soft assumption = premissa frágil: pouco sustentada, vulnerável a questionamento.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When targets are unrealistic, the process becomes an ___ that everyone resents."
items.why: Administrative ritual = ritual administrativo: exercício vazio que ninguém leva a sério.

items.q: "Two figures were adjusted quietly between drafts." This means they were…
items.why: To adjust quietly = ajustar silenciosamente: mudar sem avisar, sem que ninguém perceba.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em revisões de orçamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the final budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "James pushed back on the revised revenue target." He…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let's firm up that assumption before we approve." To firm up means to…
options: keep it as a rough guess
make it more solid and better supported
items.why: Firm up = consolidar, tornar mais robusto e sustentado.

items.q: "The team agreed the plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Trimming that line item won't move the needle on the deficit." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
